body: I sent a PR with a fix. https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/116299

Further investigation of the root cause of the bug:

On shutdown, the `AudioServer` still has a reference to an `AudioStreamPlaybackMicrophone` in its `playback_list` (of type `SafeList<AudioStreamPlaybackListNode *>`).

Typically these references to deleted `AudioStreamPlayback` objects are cleaned up within the `AudioServer::update()` call but, during shutdown, there is no `AudioServer::update()` call between the node cleanup and `AudioServer` cleanup. This means that the last reference to the `AudioStreamPlaybackMicrophone` will be cleaned up in the `AudioServer` cleanup code, most of which fires after the singleton is set to null.

`AudioStreamPlaybackMicrophone` is one of the types that, upon cleanup, need access to the AudioServer singleton, which is now null, causing a null pointer de-reference.

For clarity, this is the order of events:
- `AudioStreamPlaybackMicrophone` is playing on an `AudioStreamPlayer` object. Both `AudioStreamPlayer` and `AudioServer` own a reference to it.
- Shutdown begins.
- `AudioStreamPlayer` is destroyed. Only `AudioServer` owns a reference to `AudioStreamPlaybackMicrophone` now.
- `AudioServer` singleton is set to nullptr.
- `AudioServer` loses the last reference to the `AudioStreamPlaybackMicrophone`.
- `AudioStreamPlaybackMicrophone` is cleaned up, and attempts to access the `AudioServer` singleton through a null pointer.
- Crash.

I think I'm going to change my PR to ensure `AudioServer` references to `AudioStreamPlayback` objects are cleaned up after the scene is cleaned up, but before the `AudioServer` is destroyed.
